text:
marta: FYI — I tightened egress ACLs in prod VPCs at 06:12 to meet the new compliance baseline. After the change, KMS decryption errors and logship failures started spiking. GPU node pool autoscaler is stalling; about 30% of new nodes are stuck in Provisioning. tagging @jonathan @alyssa for visibility

jonathan: on it. can you paste the exact commands you ran? did this touch the privatelink or keystore ranges?

marta: ran these two commands from my laptop (applied to sg-0abc in prod):
```bash
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/8
```
I assumed our keystore traffic goes over privatelink but logs show a lot of outgoing TLS to public keystore-proxy.hosted.redwood.com and S3 endpoints.

alyssa: that'd explain it. logship and the keystore proxy use public egress for a subset of regions right now. logs: `Decrypt failed: AccessDenied` and `Connect timed out` for the keystore proxy.

security: we rolled the egress lockdown to meet a compliance audit — the intention was to block wide internet access. we didn't expect some control-plane helpers to use public egress. we need an exception process.

sam: autoscaler note: node bootstrap contacts the control-plane auth and keystore during init. if keystore -> public egress fails, the start script bails and the instance stays in Provisioning rather than Ready. quick mitigation is to whitelist the keystore proxy IPs + s3 endpoints for the node SG. can we do that temporarily?

marta: opening temporary exception now — adding outbound allow to the keystore proxy / s3 hostnames. doing minimal ip-level allow: 13.33.33.0/24 and s3 endpoints (presigned flows). will monitor.

deploy-bot: Rollback action executed by marta: security-group sg-0abc egress updated to allow 13.33.33.0/24 and s3.amazonaws.com. action_id=rb-20240414-01 timestamp=1728000300

jonathan: nodes are moving out of Provisioning and GPU pools are coming back online. provisioning failures dropped to <2% after the exception. however SIEM/audit shows ~200k denied egress events during the lockdown window — that spikes alerting and index/storage costs.

alyssa: long term: route keystore and critical control-plane endpoints over privatelink in eu-west and us-west. that avoids public egress and keeps the lockstep compliance posture. filing eng-platform task.

ops-squad: ENGPLAT-4123 created to add privatelink for keystore + agreed s3 presigned proxy in prod regions. P1 for Dedicated regions.

security: we need to document an approved-exceptions roster and a retention/sampling change for denied-eject audit logs. also saw some KMS key-access anomalies (cross-account attempts) in the same window — we'll open an investigation ticket.

marta: agreed. immediate follow-ups: 1) roll-forward a stricter-but-not-breaking egress baseline that allows known keystore/s3 ranges, 2) add an e2e test in staging that simulates egress lockdown to catch bootstrap breaks, 3) update the runbook with a quick rollback command.

marta: runbook snippet for fast rollback (use this when Provisioning > 10%):
```bash
# quick permissive egress to unblock node bootstrap
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 13.33.33.0/24
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --description "temp-until-privatelink"
# then monitor: kubectl get nodes --selector=role=gpu | grep NotReady
```

alyssa: thanks. also let's add cost guardrails: when denied-event count > 50k in 1h, auto-suppress noisy SIEM alerts and create a retrospective ticket so we don't burn storage.

security: noted. will coordinate with SOC to add sampling and an exception approval flow.

marta: thanks all — marking this thread resolved for now. will follow up on ENGPLAT-4123 and the security ticket. :white_check_mark:
